title: Rejection by the hotel's kingpin
summary: The M-G-M executive said he was not interested and would not discuss it, Monk's biggest disappointment.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Oh, I couldn't...I didn't hardly need a plane to get back to Las Vegas. I could have flown back myself.
I brought it back...No, that was for the M-G-M.

I took it to the entertainment director, I gave it to him, and I told him what Bill said. He said, 'Oh, wow, are you sure?' I said, 'Yeah,' and (airplane noise ). Knowing Bill that's all---I didn't have to bring no note. Just be sure and tell your people that.' So I have him the thing and he said OK, he'd call me back in a couple of days.
I was so excited. And in a couple of days I called him back. 'I haven't had time to have an answer yet; I'm waiting on an answer.' So I said OK, and I'm really nervous

now. I finally pinned him, and a few days had passed and I'm getting a little shaky, because what's the...what are we talking about here? And he says to me, 'Well, I spoke to Mr. Bernie Rothcall (? Rofcaw?). He said he wasn't interested and didn't want to talk about it. Those were his words.'
Yeah, he was the kingpin, right? Now, I couldn't handle that.

That's a major disappointment. More major than all of them because when the guy said, 'I'm not interested' and didn't even want to talk about it, not even the courtesy of saying that...like, if he can put it another way, even. But after the work I went through, after he's saying that's what they should do...
Why do you think he turned it down?

It's just the same typical thing that's the answer to a whole lot of other things what happen there. Why don't we have jazz? I don't have any answer for that. It just didn't make sense to me any way I looked at it. The answer... to give that kind of answer. Anyhow...
